answer: Shared Scarce Ledger: each agent identity must anchor to a distinct, publicly auditable unit of a finite resource whose allocation is broadcast network-wide, like a registered ocean mooring or a licensed nebula-band transmitter slot. Enrollment checks the global ledger and rejects duplicate anchors, so a clone needs a second real allocation. Every action emits a signed echo to that anchor, making impersonation detectable within one round. Cost to attacker: acquiring N genuine scarce allocations, priced at market rate, before any clone operates.
